title: Plant
description: One plant record for the static plant database. Mirrors backend/app/models/plant.py and the create_plant_tables/add_taxonomy_climate_succession_fields_and_pest_interactions Alembic migrations: top-level fields map to the `plant` table, nested arrays/objects map to the satellite tables (plant_data_source, seed_info, plant_period, plant_companion, plant_bedding_need, plant_pest_interaction). See docs/schema.md for the full ER model. Every plant is one file: data/plants/<slug>.json.

slug.description: Primary key. URL-safe, unique, e.g. 'tomato', 'sweet-basil'. Must match the file's own name (<slug>.json).

family.description: Taxonomic family, e.g. 'Solanaceae'. Used for rotation/succession-family logic.

genus.description: Taxonomic genus, e.g. 'Solanum'. Kept separate from botanical_name so rotation queries don't have to parse it back out.

min_temperature_c.description: Natural habitat temperature range, not a US hardiness zone.

edible_parts.description: e.g. ['fruit', 'leaves']. Open-ended, not a closed enum.

succession_enabled.description: Whether this crop can be re-sown at intervals through the season rather than once.

seed_info.description: Maps to the seed_info table (1:1 with plant). Omit entirely if nothing is known.

pretreatment.description: e.g. 'cold stratification 4 weeks', or null if none needed.

produces_viable_seeds.description: false for F1 hybrids and similar - null if unknown, not false.

periods.description: Maps to plant_period rows. Recurring annual windows (month only) - omit a period entirely rather than guessing start/end.

companions.description: Maps to plant_companion rows. companion_slug must reference another plant's slug (resolved at import time, not enforceable in JSON Schema alone) and must not equal this plant's own slug.

mechanism.description: Open-ended, e.g. 'pest-deterrent', 'nitrogen-fixing', 'allelopathy' - why the relationship holds.

pest_interactions.description: Maps to plant_pest_interaction rows. Plant-to-insect relationships - distinct from companions, which is plant-to-plant.

pest_or_insect.description: e.g. 'aphids', 'ladybugs', 'tomato hornworm' - free text, not a closed enum.

need_type.description: Open-ended, e.g. ground_cover | hilling | staking - not a closed enum.

growing_information.description: Maps to plant_growing_information rows. Long-form growing-advice text (e.g. Project Gutenberg books with a section per plant) - deliberately unstructured, unlike every other field here. Intended to later be mined for the fields no structured source covers (composting_needs, fertilizer_needs, needs_wind_cover/needs_rain_cover, seed_info.pretreatment, bedding_needs - see data/CLAUDE.md's 'Fields still needing a source'), but that extraction isn't built yet - this just holds the raw material.

copyright_status.description: e.g. 'public domain', 'CC BY-SA 4.0', 'unknown' - free text, varies too much for a closed enum.

record_type.description: 'raw' = one source's excerpt as-is. 'consolidated' = synthesized from multiple raw entries for this plant. Defaults to 'raw' if omitted.

generic_for_species.description: true if this text was written about the species/genus generically (e.g. 'pumpkins') rather than this specific cultivar, and copied into every matching cultivar's record - not cultivar-specific advice.

data_sources.description: Maps to plant_data_source rows. Every non-trivial field elsewhere in this record should be traceable to at least one entry here - see data/CLAUDE.md's sources table for what's available to cite.
